Smooth calibration curve and calibration metrics for a landmark model

Source: R/get_calibration.R
get_calibration.Rd

Estimates a smooth calibration curve for the landmark model at landmark time x_L, and summarises it with the integrated calibration index (ICI), E50 and E90.

get_calibration(x, x_L, span = 0.75)

Arguments

x

Object inheriting the class landmark, this should be the output from either fit_LME_landmark or fit_LOCF_landmark.

x_L

Numeric specifying the landmark time. This indicates which landmark model in x to use.

span

Numeric specifying the span of the stats::loess smoother (default 0.75).

Value

List containing curve, a data frame of predicted risks (predicted) and the smoothed observed risks (observed) at 100 points over the range of the predicted risks, and the calibration metrics ICI, E50 and E90.

Details

The observed risk of the event of interest (the event with event_status=1) by the horizon time is estimated for each individual with a pseudo-observation: the jackknife pseudo-value of the Aalen-Johansen estimate of the cumulative incidence of the event of interest (or of one minus the Kaplan-Meier estimate when there are no competing events) at the horizon time. The pseudo-observations are regressed on the predicted risks with a loess smoother to give the calibration curve, which accounts for censoring and competing risks. For a perfectly calibrated model the curve lies on the line y=x.

For each individual, the absolute difference between their predicted risk and the smoothed observed risk at that prediction is calculated. The ICI is the mean of these differences, and E50 and E90 are their median and 90th percentile (Austin et al., 2020, 2022). Smaller values indicate better calibration.

If the model was fitted with cross-validation, the predicted risks are the out-of-fold predictions, so the calibration is assessed on individuals who were not used to fit the models that predicted them.

References

Austin PC, Harrell FE, van Klaveren D (2020). Graphical calibration curves and the integrated calibration index (ICI) for survival models. Statistics in Medicine, 39(21), 2714-2742.

Austin PC, Putter H, Giardiello D, van Klaveren D (2022). Graphical calibration curves and the integrated calibration index (ICI) for competing risk models. Diagnostic and Prognostic Research, 6, 2.

Examples

library(Landmarking)
data(data_repeat_outcomes)
data_model_landmark_LOCF <-
  fit_LOCF_landmark(
    data_long = data_repeat_outcomes,
    x_L = c(60, 61),
    x_hor = c(65, 66),
    covariates =
      c("ethnicity", "smoking", "diabetes", "sbp_stnd", "tchdl_stnd"),
    covariates_time =
      c(rep("response_time_sbp_stnd", 4), "response_time_tchdl_stnd"),
    k = 10,
    individual_id = "id",
    event_time = "event_time",
    event_status = "event_status",
    survival_submodel = "cause_specific"
  )
